subject: Compute journey & subprocessor evidence request — FintechX compliance review
messages:
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@fintechx.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence needed: where compute runs and who processes EU customer data

Hi Rafael,

We're in the middle of a compliance intake for a potential deployment of Redwood for some EU-facing payment flows. Procurement/security have asked for a concise but evidentiary response to two items:

1) Exactly where request processing and model execution occur (regions / clouds) for customers who select EU-only residency. Are there any possible transient hops or third-party POPs that would touch data outside the EU?
2) Full list of subprocessors that may have access to logs or transient data, and whether any of those subprocessors are outside the EU.

Can you point me to a short statement we can share with FintechX legal + procurement, and any supporting artifacts (region matrix, subprocessor CSV, sample network trace)? The review team needs something by EOD Wednesday to keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

Sam
Sam Wilson
Security Lead, FintechX
sam.wilson@fintechx.com
+1 415-555-0199

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence needed: where compute runs and who processes EU customer data

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a short region matrix and our current subprocessor inventory to this thread (see attachments below). High-level summary for an EU-residency deployment:

- Primary execution locations: For EU-residency customers we pin inference to eu-west-1 (Ireland) or europe-west1 (Belgium) depending on region and capacity. Those are the endpoints where model execution and KV cache are instantiated.
- Transit and transient hops: Network egress for third-party services (monitoring, analytics) is minimized. There are two classes of transient hops to be aware of:
  • Control-plane metadata (deployment signals, billing events) may traverse Redwood control plane hosted in us-east-1 for hosted accounts unless the customer chooses Private (VPC) deployment. These control-plane events do not include customer input or model outputs.
  • Short-lived TLS connections to global CDNs or partner POPs for edge ingress (used only for connection handoff, not model execution or persistent storage). We operate POPs in EU regions where possible; when traffic originates from outside the EU the connection may enter through a non-EU POP but requests are routed to the pinned EU execution pool for processing.
- Subprocessors: See attached CSV (subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv). Short list includes: AWS (eu-west-1), Google Cloud (europe-west1), Equinix Metal (EU POps), Cloudflare (edge), Datadog (monitoring), Sentry (error telemetry). Only AWS/GCP/Equinix handle compute or storage where customer data may be material; Cloudflare/Datadog/Sentry receive limited telemetry or aggregated logs.
- Encryption & access controls: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+/mutual-TLS where configured. At rest we encrypt with KMS; access is role-based and audited. We can provide redacted logs showing no plaintext crossing to non-EU locations for pinned EU tenants.
- Retention/deletion: Customer content (requests + KV cache entries) is deleted on a customer-requested wipe within 72 hours from the delete API call for hosted EU tenants; cached prefixes and transient logs are purged on a 30-day rolling schedule unless otherwise contracted. Audit logs and backups are retained subject to SLA (retention windows vary; see matrix).

Attachments: redwood_region_matrix_v2.xlsx, subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv (small CSV listing subprocessors and region scopes). I also attached a short network-trace-sample.txt that illustrates a request path through a EU POP into the eu-west-1 execution pool.

If you need an explicit one-paragraph statement for procurement/legal that asserts that model execution for EU-residency customers remains inside EU compute and that subprocessors listed for EU customers are EU-based, we can provide that signed by our Privacy Officer. Would you like that on company letterhead?

Best,
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence needed: where compute runs and who processes EU customer data

Rafael / Connor — a couple of internal notes to include in the evidence pack before we finalize for Sam:

1) Add a per-region subprocessors table: list each subprocessor row-scoped to "EU-only" vs "global" and include their corporate HQ and data-center region. The CSV already has most fields but a one-page summary is helpful.
2) Include a redacted telemetry sample that shows IP provenance + final execution locus; the network-trace-sample.txt is good as an example, but redact internal hostnames.
3) For procurement we should include a concise statement about control plane metadata (explicitly call out that control plane signals may transit US-hosted control plane and do not contain customer content). That reduces surprise.
4) Confirm deletion SLA language: the hosted EU residency default should be documented as "customer content purge within 72 hours of delete request; logs retained 30 days unless otherwise contracted." Suggest we offer 7-day SLA option for customers who require longer confirmation windows.

I'll draft the one-paragraph letterhead statement and a single-slide summary for procurement. Rafael — do you want me to send the letterhead note directly to Sam or should we route through you?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@fintechx.com>

Rafael — thanks, that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications so procurement can sign off:  

1) For EU-residency customers, can you confirm in writing that model execution and any persistent storage of customer content will not be replicated or backed up to non-EU regions? (We understand control-plane metadata may transit non-EU, per your note.)
2) If you could attach the one-paragraph, company-letterhead assertion referencing the subprocessor CSV and region matrix, procurement will slot it into the contract addendum.

If you can get that to me by Wednesday EOD our procurement timeline stays on track. Appreciate it.

Sam
